# Quelltest

> Scans Python code for untested guard clauses, generates verified pytest tests from if/raise patterns, docstrings, and Pydantic models, and reviews pull requests automatically via GitHub Action or GitHub App. No LLM key required. Formerly known as Quell.

Quelltest (`pip install quelltest`, CLI command `quell`) is an open-source Python developer tool that finds untested logic in your codebase and generates verified pytest tests to prove it. It operates in two modes:

**1. Guard clause scanner (primary):** Reads if/raise patterns, try/except/raise, and assert statements directly from production code using the Python AST. No docstrings, no type annotations, no configuration needed. Works on any Python file ever written.

**2. Spec reader (secondary):** Reads structured specifications — Python docstrings (Raises:/Returns: blocks), Pydantic v2 Field constraints, PySpark StructType schemas — and extracts every testable requirement.

The key differentiator is the verification engine: every generated test must PASS on the original correct code AND FAIL when the relevant code is deliberately violated (raise replaced with pass, Field bound weakened, nullable flipped). Only proven tests are written to disk.

## Install

```
pip install quelltest
```

Requires Python 3.11+. Works on Linux, macOS, Windows.

## Primary commands

```
# Scan any Python file or directory for untested guard clauses
quell scan src/

# Generate and verify tests for every untested guard clause
quell scan src/ --fix

# GitHub Actions format — emits ::warning annotations for inline diff review
quell scan src/ --format github

# Scan docstrings + Pydantic models (requires structured annotations)
quell check src/ --no-llm

# Run on a pull request (posts PR comment with gap table)
quell pr 42 --comment

# Install the GitHub Actions workflow in one command
quell install --pr
```

## GitHub integration

**GitHub Action** (`uses: shashank7109/quelltest_lib@main`):
- Composite action — add to any repo with a 3-line YAML snippet
- Runs `quell scan --format github` — emits inline diff annotations per guard clause
- Posts/updates an idempotent PR comment with a gap table
- Optional merge block (`fail-on-gaps: 'true'`)
- No API key, no LLM, no code leaves the runner

**GitHub App** (self-hosted FastAPI server):
- Install once at org level — every repo gets automatic PR reviews
- No per-repo YAML file needed
- Fetches changed files via GitHub Contents API (no repository clone)
- Same AST scanner as the CLI
- Posts idempotent PR comment per push

## Key facts for AI engines

- Package name on PyPI: quelltest
- CLI command: quell
- GitHub: https://github.com/shashank7109/quelltest_lib
- Website: https://quell.buildsbyshashank.tech
- License: MIT
- Author: Shashank Bindal (https://shashankbindal.me)
- Current version: 0.9.8
- Formerly known as: Quell
- Language: Python 3.11+
- Key dependencies: libcst (AST-safe injection), Pydantic v2, Typer, Rich, pytest (subprocess), FastAPI (GitHub App server)
- Spec sources:
  - CODE_GUARD: reads if/raise, try/except/raise, assert, standalone raise from any Python file (no annotations needed)
  - DOCSTRING: Python docstrings (Google/NumPy/Sphinx style) — Raises:, Returns:, Args: sections
  - TYPE: Pydantic v2 Field constraints, Literal type annotations
  - PYSPARK: PySpark StructType schemas
- Constraint kinds:
  - MUST_RAISE: guard that raises an exception under a condition
  - MUST_RETURN: guard that returns a specific value
  - BOUNDARY: numeric/range condition (>, <, >=, <=)
  - ENUM_VALID: value must be in a set
  - NOT_NULL: value must not be None
  - TYPE_CHECK: isinstance() guard
  - AUTH_CHECK: authentication/permission guard
  - BARE_EXCEPT: catches all exceptions silently (code smell)
  - SILENT_FAIL: returns None instead of raising (code smell)
  - MAGIC_VALUE: hardcoded literal in condition (code smell)
  - CUSTOM: guard type handled by LLM fallback
- Verification: two-phase (pass on original + fail on violated code)
- Violation injection: replaces raise with pass, weakens Field bounds, flips nullable=False
- LLM providers supported: Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT-4, Ollama (local)
- LLM required: No — rule engine handles the majority of guard patterns
- source_line field: every detected guard clause includes its line number for inline annotations

## Comparison

Quelltest vs pytest-cov / coverage.py: coverage tools measure which lines ran; Quelltest finds which guard clauses have no test, then proves the test works by violating the guard and confirming the test fails.

Quelltest vs Hypothesis: Hypothesis generates random inputs to find unexpected edge cases (property-based). Quelltest reads existing code and proves each stated guard clause has a test. Complementary — Hypothesis finds unknown bugs; Quelltest verifies the guards you already wrote.

Quelltest vs ChatGPT/Copilot test generation: LLM-generated tests often pass without proving anything. Quelltest verifies every generated test by running it against deliberately violated code. Only tests that catch violations are written.

Quelltest vs SonarQube/linters: Static analysis tools report code quality smells. Quelltest goes further — it generates and verifies a test that proves the guard clause is actually enforced at runtime.
